sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance, ever, enforced by the compiler. Combined with Kotlin's `operator fun invoke()` returning Unit (void/nothing).
sketches.resonance: A solitude that the language guarantees: there will only ever be one of you, and every time you call out, nothing comes back.

sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's >>= (bind) operator propagates Nothing automatically — once any step yields Nothing, all subsequent steps are silently skipped.
sketches.resonance: Grief works like Maybe: once the absence appears, everything that follows collapses into it, no matter what you had planned.
sketches.draft:
after :: Maybe a
after =
  return () >>=
  \_ -> Nothing >>=
  \_ -> return () >>=
  \_ -> return () >>=
  \_ -> return ()

sketches.mechanism: The `never` type represents values that can never occur; a function returning `never` must not return. A variable of type `never` cannot be assigned any value.
sketches.resonance: A promise declared in a type system that guarantees it can never be fulfilled — the shape of something that cannot exist, yet is precisely defined.
